_readme: This file is a worksheet, not a finished map. It records every address the co-op mod
needs, what it knows about each one, and how to re-derive it on a disc we have never
seen. Nothing here is game data: the entries are addresses, byte patterns and offsets,
and the whole file is meant to be regenerated on the user's own copy.
addr       - a pinned address (only ever valid for the exact build you measured)
signature  - a byte pattern scanned for at install time, so it survives across builds
neither    - NOT FOUND YET. `aecoops doctor` lists these; docs/DISCOVERY.md has the recipes
verified   - the date someone confirmed it on hardware. null means nobody has.

ntsc-u.note: also released on PS4/PS5 as a PS2 classic; the classic is the same image

pal.note: add the serial from your own disc: `aecoops doctor` prints it, along with the CRC

ntsc-j.note: Saru Get You 3. Add the serial and CRC from your own disc.

characters._note: The two hero ids the engine stores in an actor's character field. They are small integers and almost certainly 0 and 1, but 'almost certainly' is how you corrupt a stage's models, so they stay null until measured. Recipe: docs/DISCOVERY.md#character-ids

layouts._note: Values the renderer reads to decide how many viewports to draw and how to cut them. `single` is whatever the story stage writes there today (often 0); a split value is whatever a two-viewport state writes. Note that no Ape Escape 3 minigame is known to be split-screen, so the reference is the story renderer's own secondary views (the MonkeyCam picture-in-picture, the L2 first-person zoom), not a minigame. Recipe: docs/DISCOVERY.md#view-mode

frame_hook.note: The `jal` the game executes exactly once per frame in a running stage. Everything the mod does depends on this one: it is where the interpreter gets installed. Until it is set, install() refuses to touch the game.
frame_hook.recipe: docs/DISCOVERY.md#frame-hook -- `aecoops discover sweep --from-elf <your.elf>` tests every candidate and keeps the one that ticks at frame rate.

view_mode.note: Renderer's viewport-count / layout selector. Forcing it to a split value is what gives two screens.

actor_count.note: How many player actors the stage simulates this frame. Usually recomputed from the stage's mode, so it needs re-applying every frame rather than being set once.

partner_enabled.note: Flag the stage logic reads to decide whether the second hero exists at all (as opposed to being allocated but idle).

quota_shared.note: Optional. When set, the monkey quota for the stage is shared and either hero's captures count. Leave unresolved and the mod simply does not touch it.

hud_instances.note: Optional. How many HUD instances the renderer builds this frame: 1 in a story stage, 2 in a two-player minigame. `aecoops play --hud per-view` writes 2 so each half can have its own; `--hud hidden` writes 0. Unmeasured means the mod leaves the HUD completely alone.

viewport_count.note: Optional. How many views of the world the renderer draws this frame: 1 in a story stage (plus the MonkeyCam, which is a separate picture), 2 once the split exists. The rectangle route writes it when it is measured.

monkeycam.note: The MonkeyCam picture-in-picture: the one place the story renderer is *known* to draw a second view of the world into a rectangle at runtime (L2 enlarges it, L2 restores it). Its address is not needed to run co-op -- it is the reference measurement the viewport recipe starts from.

base.note: Address of slot 0 of the player-actor table. The engine keeps two of these structures; in story mode it only ever fills slot 0.

actor._stride_note: Bytes between the two actor structures. Find it by locating the same field (a pad port is the easiest) in both slots.

active.note: Non-zero while the engine simulates this slot. Slot 1 is zeroed in story mode; the mod sets it every frame.

char_id.note: Which hero this actor is: Kei or Yumi. Writing the two ids into the two slots is the whole of 'play as either Kei or Yumi'.

pad_port.note: Which controller slot drives this actor. 0 for player one, 1 for player two.

pos_x.note: World position, in IEEE single-precision. Stored as a float: writes through the cave are raw words, so the mod never has to understand the encoding.

yaw.note: Facing. Tethered with the position so a mirrored partner looks where player one looks instead of backwards.

base.note: Slot 0 of the HUD instance table. One entry per viewport: in story mode there is one, in a two-player minigame there are two, and that difference is what makes the minigames the reference implementation for a split-screen HUD.

hud._stride_note: Bytes between two HUD instances. Find it the same way as the actor stride: the field that differs between the two players' HUDs (a score, a stamina bar, an owner index) appears twice, at the same offset, that far apart.

visible.note: Non-zero while this instance is drawn. Usually 1, but a slot the renderer skipped last frame is remembered as 0, so the mod writes it every frame.

x.note: Where the instance sits, in the game's own HUD coordinates (see `--screen`). In a vertical split the mod puts instance 1 at the left edge of the left view and instance 2 at the left edge of the right view.

owner.note: Which player's state this HUD shows -- the field the minigames set to 0 and 1 so each player reads their own score. In story mode there is one candidate state, so leave it unresolved and the mod simply does not write it.

base.note: The stage camera. Only needed to keep a split view from pointing both halves at the same hero; the engine's own two-player camera path is preferred where it exists.

target_actor.note: Which actor slot this camera follows.

base.note: Slot 0 of the viewport table: the rectangle the renderer draws view 0 into. The story stage has one; the split needs two. Start from the MonkeyCam's rectangle, which the game itself moves at runtime and therefore stores in memory rather than baking into the draw call.

viewport._stride_note: Bytes between two viewport rectangles. If the game only ever has one, this is the size of the structure: find it by looking for the next field after w/h that the renderer sets.

x.note: Rectangle left edge, in the renderer's coordinate space.

w.note: Rectangle width. In a vertical split this is half the frame.

h.note: Rectangle height. In a horizontal split this is half the frame.

target_actor.note: Optional. Which actor slot this view follows: 0 for player one, 1 for player two. Writing it is what stops both halves pointing at the same hero.
